title: Training: Buying Redwood Inference via AWS & GCP Cloud Marketplaces (Sales/SE/CS Enablement)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Buying Redwood Inference via AWS & GCP Cloud Marketplaces
Enablement for Sales / Solutions Engineering / Customer Success

Primary goals:
- Help enterprise buyers use committed spend (AWS EDP / GCP CUD) while keeping dev onboarding fast
- Reduce friction from “I can only buy via marketplace” to “you’re provisioned + live”
- Standardize what we collect, how we route, and how we escalate

Owners:
- GTM Enablement: Markus Klein (SE)
- Listings/messaging: Soojin Lee (PMM)
- Support readiness: Dev Patel / Jasmine Liu


Slide 2 — When to recommend Marketplace vs Direct Contract
Marketplace is a great fit when:
- Customer must use cloud committed spend (AWS/GCP)
- Procurement requires marketplace workflow for vendor onboarding
- Buyer wants consolidated cloud invoice + simplified PO process

Direct contract is usually better when:
- Non-standard terms required (custom DPA clauses, unusual liability language)
- Complex multi-entity billing, non-cloud payment method, or large bespoke discounting
- On-prem / air-gapped Private deployments that can’t be represented cleanly in marketplace terms

Field note:
- Do not “force” marketplace if it creates long provisioning risk. Offer both paths early.


Slide 3 — Quick SKU mental model (what the customer is actually buying)
Redwood Marketplace SKUs map to:
1) Hosted API (usage-based): fastest start, pay per token/embedding via marketplace billing
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput + isolation; commit terms represented in marketplace
3) Private (VPC / private control plane): enterprise controls; provisioning is heavier + often needs kickoff
4) Add-ons (where applicable): Compliance package, retention/observability retention, premium SLA/support

Messaging shorthand:
- Hosted = “API in minutes”
- Dedicated = “reserved GPUs with Redwood operating the stack”
- Private = “your network boundary + enterprise controls”


Slide 4 — End-to-end buyer journey (we own the handoffs)
1) Evaluate (trial / POC)
2) Select marketplace + SKU
3) Purchase in AWS/GCP marketplace
4) Entitlement created by marketplace
5) Redwood ingests entitlement → creates/updates org entitlements
6) Customer links purchase to a Redwood org (Console) / completes onboarding wizard
7) First successful API call / deployment validation

Our biggest failure points (historically):
- Entitlement delays (webhook lag / incorrect account context)
- Wrong org linked (multiple orgs, multiple cloud accounts)
- Region mismatch (customer expects EU region, entitlement defaults to US)


Slide 5 — Discovery questions (ask before the customer buys)
Collect these BEFORE sending the marketplace link:
- Cloud: AWS or GCP? (and which account/project will purchase)
- Target deployment: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Region requirement (US/EU/APAC) + any residency constraints
- Org context:
  - Does the buyer already have a Redwood org? Who is org admin?
  - Do they need a new org for this purchase?
- Security requirements: SOC 2 report request, SSO/SAML, KMS expectations, audit logs, retention controls
- Procurement constraints: PO required? invoice details? timeline to signature/purchase?

SE tip:
- If they can’t answer “which AWS account / GCP project will buy,” pause and get clarity. That’s the #1 source of mis-provisioning.


Slide 6 — What information to collect (copy/paste checklist)
Customer + purchase identifiers:
- Customer legal name (as used by procurement)
- Primary technical contact + billing/procurement contact
- Cloud:
  - AWS payer account ID (12-digit) + buyer account ID (if different)
  - OR GCP billing account + project ID that will purchase
- Intended Redwood org name + org admin email
- Desired region(s) for inference
- SKU intended + add-ons expected (compliance/retention/premium SLA)

After purchase (to speed triage):
- Marketplace purchase date/time
- Marketplace order/contract ID (AWS) or entitlement ID (GCP)
- Screenshot of purchase confirmation page (redact sensitive where needed)


Slide 7 — AWS Marketplace: buyer steps (high level)
1) Buyer locates “Redwood Inference” listing in AWS Marketplace
2) Choose the correct plan/SKU + accept terms
3) Click Subscribe / Purchase
4) AWS generates an entitlement for the buyer account
5) Buyer completes Redwood “Link your AWS Marketplace purchase” step in Console

Common AWS gotchas:
- Wrong AWS account purchased (payer vs linked account confusion)
- IAM permissions prevent completing subscription steps
- Entitlement appears but org linking hasn’t been done (customer thinks “paid = active”)


Slide 8 — GCP Marketplace: buyer steps (high level)
1) Buyer opens the “Redwood Inference” solution in Google Cloud Marketplace
2) Select plan + confirm billing account
3) Click Subscribe / Purchase
4) GCP generates entitlement tied to billing account + project context
5) Buyer completes Redwood org linking in Console

Common GCP gotchas:
- Project selected during purchase isn’t the one running workloads
- Billing account doesn’t match expectations
- Region/availability confusion (buyer expects a region that isn’t enabled for their org)


Slide 9 — Org linking: how to explain it to customers (use this script)
“After purchase, the cloud marketplace creates an entitlement. Redwood needs you to link that entitlement to the Redwood org where you want the product enabled. This is a 1–3 minute step in the Redwood Console and ensures the right team and environment get access.”

What the customer needs to have ready:
- Redwood org admin access (or invite an admin)
- The cloud account/project that purchased

If the customer wants separation:
- Recommend a dedicated Redwood org for prod vs dev, or separate business units


Slide 10 — Expected timelines + what “normal” looks like
Typical:
- Purchase → entitlement visible to Redwood: minutes
- Entitlement → org entitlement applied: minutes (automated)
- Org linking: immediate once user completes wizard

When to worry:
- >30 minutes from purchase with no entitlement showing in Console
- Repeated “entitlement not found” errors after verifying correct cloud account/project
- Region mismatch blocks provisioning

Set expectations with buyers:
- “If anything takes more than ~30 minutes, we’ll treat it as a provisioning issue and escalate.”


Slide 11 — Where to send customers (approved links / assets)
Customer-facing references (use the latest docs, not old PDFs):
- AWS Marketplace onboarding guide (docs site)
- GCP Marketplace onboarding guide (docs site)
- Marketplace Security FAQ (for procurement / security teams)

Internal references:
- CS troubleshooting guide + escalation paths
- Marketplace review checklist (for launch / listing changes)

Reminder:
- Don’t paste internal runbook links directly to customers.


Slide 12 — Common objections + talk tracks
Objection: “Marketplace is too confusing; we just want an invoice.”
- Talk track: “Marketplace lets you use committed cloud spend and consolidates billing. If that’s not required, we can do a direct contract as well.”

Objection: “We need a one-pager on security/compliance.”
- Talk track: “We have a marketplace security FAQ and can share additional evidence under NDA as needed (SOC 2 report handling).”

Objection: “We bought it. Why isn’t it active?”
- Talk track: “You’re subscribed, but you still need to link the purchase to the correct Redwood org. We can do that together in 2 minutes.”


Slide 13 — Support triage categories (what bucket is this ticket?)
Category A: Purchase/entitlement not received
- Symptoms: Console shows no entitlement, or “not found”
- Likely causes: wrong account/project, webhook lag, validation failure

Category B: Wrong org linked / need transfer
- Symptoms: entitlement applied to wrong org, user can’t see entitlement
- Likely causes: multiple orgs, admin linked wrong one

Category C: Region mismatch / availability
- Symptoms: entitlement exists but provisioning blocked by region policy
- Likely causes: org region settings, SKU region constraints

Category D: Billing/invoice confusion
- Symptoms: invoice descriptors, usage meter questions, refunds/credits expectations
- Likely causes: marketplace billing model differences vs direct contract


Slide 14 — Troubleshooting flow (SE/CS quick decision tree)
Step 1: Confirm cloud + purchase context
- AWS: which account ID purchased? payer vs linked?
- GCP: which billing account + which project?

Step 2: Confirm Redwood org details
- Org name + org admin email
- Is the user in the right org?

Step 3: Check entitlement status in Console
- “Pending” vs “Active” vs “Not found”

Step 4: Basic remediation
- If wrong org: guide admin to relink (or open internal request if transfer requires support)
- If region mismatch: confirm target region; capture requirement; route to Eng/Platform if policy change needed

Step 5: Escalate if still blocked >30 min
- Use escalation checklist (next slides)


Slide 15 — Escalation playbook (internal)
When to escalate to Engineering (marketplace provisioning):
- Entitlement not ingested after 30 minutes AND account/project is confirmed
- Repeated webhook validation failures / idempotency errors
- Multiple customers affected (potential incident)

When to escalate to SRE:
- Elevated webhook failure rate
- Entitlement lag dashboard indicates backlog
- Any symptoms of partial outage

When to escalate to Finance/Legal:
- Customer requests refund/credit explanation tied to marketplace policy
- Invoice line-item naming disputes that require official statement
- Non-standard terms questions


Slide 16 — Escalation checklist (what to include so Eng can act fast)
Include all of the below in Slack/Jira escalation:
- Cloud: AWS or GCP
- Purchase identifier:
  - AWS: order/contract ID + buyer AWS account ID
  - GCP: entitlement ID + billing account + project ID
- Timestamp of purchase (timezone)
- Redwood org ID/name + org admin email
- SKU expected + add-ons expected
- Region requirement
- Screenshots/logs:
  - Console entitlement screen
  - Any error messages (exact copy)

Bad escalation: “customer can’t onboard”
Good escalation: “AWS entitlement not ingested 45 min after purchase; buyer acct 1234…; order id …; org ‘Acme-Prod’; console error ‘entitlement not found’; need EU-West routing”


Slide 17 — Customer-facing status updates (templates)
Template 1 — Acknowledge + set expectations
“Thanks — we see your subscription. The next step is linking the marketplace entitlement to your Redwood org. If it doesn’t activate within ~30 minutes after purchase, we’ll escalate and keep you updated.”

Template 2 — Collect missing info
“To troubleshoot, can you confirm the AWS account ID (or GCP billing account + project) used to purchase, and the Redwood org name you want to enable?”

Template 3 — Escalation in progress
“We’re escalating this to our provisioning/onboarding engineering team now. Next update in 60 minutes or sooner; if you can share the marketplace order/entitlement ID, it will help us resolve faster.”


Slide 18 — Dedicated vs Private: how to guide SKU selection (field guidance)
Dedicated
- Best when: predictable throughput, isolation, but customer is OK with Redwood-managed infra boundary
- Talk track: “Reserved capacity with SLOs; fastest path to predictable performance.”

Private
- Best when: VPC boundary, customer-managed networking, regulated workloads
- Talk track: “Private control plane + stronger network isolation; longer setup, but enterprise controls.”

Warning signs to clarify early:
- “We need on-prem / air-gapped” → likely not a standard marketplace-only workflow
- “We need data residency in EU only” → confirm supported regions and document language


Slide 19 — Security/Compliance: what we can and can’t promise
Do:
- Use approved security FAQ language
- Describe encryption in transit/at rest, audit logging availability, SSO options at a high level
- Offer SOC 2 report under appropriate process (NDA as required)

Don’t:
- Promise “HIPAA compliant” or “FedRAMP” unless explicitly approved for that SKU and documented
- Overstate logging/retention (“full packet capture” etc.)
- Commit to customer-specific controls in writing without Security/Legal review

Escalation path for security questionnaires:
- Naomi Feldman (PM security reqs) → Marcus Lin (SecEng controls accuracy) → Olga Petrov (GRC evidence)


Slide 20 — Metrics we care about (so we can improve)
Track (internal):
- Marketplace lead → purchase conversion
- Purchase → entitlement active (p50/p95)
- Purchase → first successful request
- Ticket rate per 100 marketplace purchases
- Top root causes (wrong account, wrong org, region mismatch, billing confusion)

Where to log feedback:
- Add notes in account record + tag “marketplace-onboarding”
- If systemic: post in #partnerships + #support with details


Slide 21 — Live demo flow (optional for training)
Demo steps (5–7 min):
1) Show listing (AWS or GCP) and point out plan selection
2) Show Redwood Console “Link Marketplace Purchase” screen
3) Show entitlement state: Pending → Active
4) Show “validate install” / first API call
5) Show where to find troubleshooting + support contact

What to emphasize:
- Linking to the correct org
- Region selection
- Where the customer sees status (reduce “black box” anxiety)


Slide 22 — Roles & RACI (who does what?)
Sales (AE):
- Qualify procurement need (marketplace vs direct)
- Confirm cloud + purchasing account/project
- Align SKU + get procurement/billing contacts

Solutions Engineering:
- Guide selection (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), help with org linking, validate first request
- Own technical triage until it’s clearly a product/provisioning defect

Customer Success / Support:
- Own ticket intake + comms once customer is live or if issues require support tooling
- Use standard macros + ensure escalation payload is complete

Partnerships:
- Own listing changes + partner communications (not day-to-day onboarding tickets)


Slide 23 — Appendix: “Before you send the marketplace link” checklist
- [ ] Confirm AWS account ID / GCP billing account + project
- [ ] Confirm Redwood org name + admin
- [ ] Confirm target region + any residency constraints
- [ ] Confirm SKU + add-ons
- [ ] Send customer the correct onboarding doc link (AWS vs GCP)
- [ ] Set expectation: purchase + org linking required; escalation if >30 minutes


Slide 24 — Appendix: Known issues / edge cases (as of last update)
- Multiple AWS linked accounts under one payer: buyer accidentally purchases in wrong linked account
- GCP: buyer purchases under a “sandbox” project but expects prod org access
- Customer with multiple Redwood orgs: entitlement linked to dev org by mistake
- Region mismatch: customer requires EU but org defaults to US routing; needs policy update

If you hit an edge case not listed:
- Capture the identifiers + timestamps and post in #support + tag SE on-call


Slide 25 — Close
If you remember 3 things:
1) Get the right cloud account/project BEFORE purchase
2) Org linking is a required step—make it explicit
3) Escalate with full identifiers; don’t escalate vague
